_meta.topic: Vehicle state estimation and identification using Kalman filtering methods
_meta.note: All data is fabricated for demonstration purposes.

topic: Vehicle state estimation and identification using Kalman filtering methods
user_direction: Developing a novel adaptive Kalman filtering approach for real-time vehicle state estimation using multi-sensor fusion on commercial vehicles

theme_clusters.label: Vehicle Dynamics State Estimation
theme_clusters.gap_description: Most focus on passenger vehicles with standard sensor configurations; limited work on commercial vehicles with heterogeneous sensor suites

theme_clusters.label: Machine Learning for Vehicle Diagnostics
theme_clusters.gap_description: ML approaches used for component diagnostics but rarely integrated with traditional Kalman-based state estimation frameworks

theme_clusters.label: Navigation and Positioning for Autonomous Vehicles
theme_clusters.gap_description: Navigation focus with limited attention to vehicle body dynamics estimation; opportunity to bridge navigation and dynamics estimation

theme_clusters.label: Component Degradation and Remaining Life Estimation
theme_clusters.gap_description: Traditional statistical approaches dominate; no integration with real-time state estimation methods

theme_clusters.label: Kalman Filter Variants Comparison and Tuning
theme_clusters.gap_description: Comparative studies exist but lack systematic framework for method selection based on vehicle type and operating conditions

structure_patterns.label: Standard Russian 5-Chapter (Introduction + Review + Methods + Experiments + Conclusion)
structure_patterns.notes: Most common structure for Russian engineering candidate dissertations in vehicle dynamics

structure_patterns.label: Extended Russian 6-Chapter (with separate Theory chapter)
structure_patterns.notes: Common when mathematical modeling is a significant contribution; separates theoretical foundations from algorithm development

structure_patterns.label: International 6-Chapter (with Discussion chapter)
structure_patterns.notes: Western-style structure with explicit discussion chapter; found in Zotero-collected international theses

structure_patterns.label: Minimal 4-Chapter (Review + Methods + Results + Conclusion)
structure_patterns.notes: Compressed structure; often signals narrower scope or shorter dissertations

validation_patterns.label: Simulation → Real Vehicle Validation
validation_patterns.description: Algorithm development and initial validation via MATLAB/Simulink or CarSim simulation, followed by real vehicle testing with data acquisition systems
validation_patterns.typical_claims: Method achieves X% accuracy improvement over baseline on real vehicle data

validation_patterns.label: Simulation → Test Bench Validation
validation_patterns.description: Simulation-based development followed by validation on a hardware-in-the-loop test bench or vehicle component test stand
validation_patterns.typical_claims: Bench results confirm simulation predictions within X% deviation

validation_patterns.label: Simulation-Only Validation
validation_patterns.description: All validation conducted via numerical simulation; no physical experiments
validation_patterns.typical_claims: Algorithm converges within X iterations with Y% accuracy in simulation

validation_patterns.label: Purely Experimental Validation
validation_patterns.description: Method developed and validated entirely through physical experiments without prior simulation

validation_patterns.label: Comparative Algorithm Analysis
validation_patterns.description: Systematic comparison of multiple algorithms under identical conditions
validation_patterns.typical_claims: Algorithm A outperforms Algorithm B by X% under condition Y

positioning_gaps.description: Only 1 of 18 analyzed dissertations focuses on commercial/heavy vehicles; the overwhelming majority address passenger cars
positioning_gaps.recommendation: Position thesis around heavy commercial vehicle state estimation — underrepresented and practically important

positioning_gaps.description: Kalman filtering and ML are used separately; no dissertation combines adaptive KF tuning with ML-based process noise estimation
positioning_gaps.recommendation: Develop hybrid KF+ML approach where ML optimizes KF parameters in real-time

positioning_gaps.description: Most dissertations validate offline; few demonstrate real-time embedded implementation on vehicle ECUs
positioning_gaps.recommendation: Include embedded system implementation and real-time performance analysis

positioning_gaps.description: Most validation is under normal driving conditions; extreme conditions (ice, heavy rain, off-road) are rarely addressed
positioning_gaps.recommendation: Test under diverse operating conditions including adverse weather and road surfaces

borrowable_moves.description: Open the introduction with industry statistics on road safety / accident rates, then narrow to the specific technical gap that the thesis addresses
Include a comparison table of candidate methods with criteria (accuracy, computational cost, robustness, implementation complexity) to justify the chosen approach
Present algorithm convergence plots (estimation error vs. time) as the primary result metric before discussing absolute accuracy
Decompose total estimation error into sensor noise contribution, model mismatch contribution, and algorithmic error to show which dominates
State contributions in a numbered list of 3 items: (1) new mathematical model, (2) new algorithm, (3) experimental validation with quantified improvements

risk_warnings.description: Kalman filtering (EKF/UKF) is used in 65% of dissertations in this domain. Pure KF application without novelty may be seen as insufficient contribution.
risk_warnings.mitigation: Differentiate through hybrid KF+ML approach, adaptive tuning, or application to an underrepresented vehicle class (commercial vehicles)

risk_warnings.description: The field increasingly expects both simulation AND real vehicle validation. Simulation-only validation may be viewed as insufficient by reviewers.
risk_warnings.mitigation: Plan for real vehicle testing from the start; budget time for experimental validation

risk_warnings.description: Topic is very close to 5+ recent dissertations focused on passenger vehicles. Risk of being perceived as incremental work.
risk_warnings.mitigation: Explicitly differentiate by focusing on commercial vehicles, novel sensor configurations, or real-time embedded implementation

risk_warnings.description: Covering all vehicle states (longitudinal, lateral, yaw, roll, pitch) plus all Kalman variants may be too broad for a single dissertation.
risk_warnings.mitigation: Focus on 2–3 key states and 1–2 KF variants; save others for future work

recommended_outline.title: Обзор современных методов оценки состояния транспортных средств. Постановка задачи исследования
recommended_outline.rationale: Standard first chapter in 90% of Russian engineering dissertations; addresses positioning gap by surveying the field and stating the problem

recommended_outline.title: Математическая модель динамики коммерческого транспортного средства
recommended_outline.rationale: Theory chapter present in 75% of corpus; needed to establish the vehicle dynamics model used throughout the thesis

recommended_outline.title: Адаптивный алгоритм оценки состояния на основе гибридного KF-ML подхода
recommended_outline.rationale: Core contribution chapter; the hybrid KF+ML method addresses the methodology gap identified in the landscape

recommended_outline.title: Имитационное моделирование и анализ сходимости алгоритма
recommended_outline.rationale: Simulation results chapter; addresses convergence analysis borrowable move; expected by 85% of corpus

recommended_outline.title: Экспериментальная верификация на реальном коммерческом транспортном средстве
recommended_outline.rationale: Experimental validation chapter; addresses validation gap (most dissertations use simulation only for commercial vehicles); differentiates thesis

recommended_outline.title: Заключение и направления дальнейших исследований
recommended_outline.rationale: Standard final chapter; present in 100% of corpus

evidence_needed: Systematic comparison table of existing methods with quantitative metrics
Statistics on commercial vehicle accidents/state estimation needs
Gap analysis supported by citation count data
Convergence proof or analysis for the proposed algorithm
Comparison with baseline methods on benchmark scenarios
Statistical significance tests for improvement claims
Real vehicle test data with sensor specifications
Comparison tables: simulation vs. experimental results
Embedded system performance metrics (latency, memory usage)
